ociUrl.description: OCI URL of the Generic `agent` chart every agent renders from (2.x: one release renders one api.kagent.dev/v1alpha3 Agent plus the agent's muster RemoteMCPServer). Written into the shared per-namespace OCIRepository, and read at run time for the chart's values.schema.json that validates every create/update before it is applied (the pod needs egress to this registry; the embedded copy of the schema is the offline fallback).

refresh.description: How often the registry is re-read for the latest version and schema.

semver.description: Semver range the OCIRepository tracks. `2.x` follows every 2.x release of the Generic chart and never a pre-release build or a next major.

semverFilter.description: Regular expression the chart's tags must match before `semver` is evaluated (the OCIRepository's ref.semverFilter, and the version the values schema is read from). Set it beside a range that admits pre-releases (`>=1.5.0-0 <2.0.0-0`): the chart's branch builds are pushed to the same repository, and `^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-rc\.[0-9]+)?$` keeps them out while admitting release candidates. Empty filters nothing.

helmReleaseApiVersion.description: helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io API version composed into HelmReleases; `auto` discovers it.

helmReleaseServiceAccount.description: HelmRelease.spec.serviceAccountName, required by a Flux multi-tenancy admission policy in tenant namespaces; empty omits it.

ociRepositoryApiVersion.description: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io API version composed into OCIRepositories; `auto` discovers it.

ociRepositoryInterval.description: OCIRepository.spec.interval of the shared chart source.

fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully qualified release name (the umbrella chart pins the Service name through this).

apiURL.description: GitHub's REST API, for `GET /user` and the pull request.

authorizationEndpoint.description: GitHub's authorize endpoint (GitHub publishes no discovery document).

name.description: Secret with the App's OAuth client under `client-id` and `client-secret`.

namespace.description: Namespace of that Secret; empty is the release namespace.

expectedIssuer.description: The issuer GitHub puts in the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter of its authorization response, `https://github.com/login/oauth` for every App. Empty omits the field.

grantScope.description: `subject`: the grant belongs to the person, not to one login session.

issuer.description: The issuer identity the person's grant is filed under: the App's own, so the login App's GitHub grant stays separate. Also passed to the server, which names it in its refusals.

scopes.description: The OAuth `scope` parameter, only for an authorization server that needs one (a lab's stand-in); empty for GitHub, whose App permissions are the App's. Empty omits the field.

enabled.description: Register with muster pinned to the GitHub App `giantswarm-agent-manager` and offer commit mode (`mode: commit` on `create_agent`, `update_agent` and `delete_agent`: the manifests land as a pull request opened as the person in the repository that owns the namespace). The MCPServer's auth then pins the App as the authorization server: muster runs the App's consent once per person and puts their user token on every call, which this server verifies with `GET /user` and opens the pull request with, and sets `forwardIdentity: true`, so muster forwards the person's IdP ID token in `X-Muster-Id-Token` next to it and apply mode keeps acting on Kubernetes as the person. Needs `oauth.enabled`, and the App installed with contents and pull-request write on every repository a commit may target. Off: muster forwards the ID token as the bearer (`muster.mcpServer.auth.forwardToken`) and commit mode answers `unsupported`.

name.description: Name of the platform Harness an agent runs on unless `create_agent` names another (the connectivity chart renders it): composed as the chart value `agent.harness`, the Agent's `spec.harnessRef.name`.

enabled.description: Expose the service through a Gateway API HTTPRoute.

parentRefs.description: parentRefs of the HTTPRoute (required when enabled).

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart appVersion.

additionalNamespaces.description: Additional namespaces agents may live in (multi-tenant installs). Each gets the same Role; requests naming any other namespace are refused.

apiVersion.description: api.kagent.dev API version for Agents, Harnesses, RemoteMCPServers and ModelConfigs; `auto` discovers the version serving `agents` (default v1alpha3).

controllerTarget.description: The kagent controller's gRPC API through agentgateway, which `list_sessions`, `get_session` and `start_session` call as the caller (SessionService and the A2A service, the caller's IdP token as the bearer): `grpc://host:port` (h2c, the in-cluster agentgateway Service) or `grpcs://host[:port]` (TLS). Rendered only with `oauth.enabled`, since the calls never run as the ServiceAccount; empty turns the session tools off (`get_info` capabilities.sessions). With `networkPolicy.enabled` the policy opens egress to it: the Service's namespace for an in-cluster host, every address otherwise.

namespace.description: Namespace agents are created in and listed from by default — the namespace the kagent controller watches, the platform admin provisions ModelConfigs into and the connectivity chart renders the platform Harness into. The Role for HelmReleases, OCIRepositories, Agents, RemoteMCPServers, Harnesses, ModelConfigs and events is created here.

enabled.description: Serve the MCP streamable-HTTP endpoint alongside the REST API.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to this server; rendered only with `oauth.enabled`. `forwardToken` makes muster forward the session's IdP id_token byte-identical (the SSO path this chart trusts through its trusted audiences). `requiredAudiences` are extra audiences that token must carry — the Dex cross-client audience the kube-apiserver trusts (`dex-k8s-authenticator` on Giant Swarm clusters; agentlab's is `kubernetes`) so `oauth.downstream` works; muster requests them at login, so users re-login after a change. They are trusted as bearer audiences by construction, since the server's trusted audiences are `oauth.trustedAudiences` plus this list. A Google IdP has no cross-client audiences: leave the list empty.

autoStart.description: Start the server connection when muster initializes.

enabled.description: Register this server with muster by rendering an `mcpservers.muster.giantswarm.io` CR in the release namespace. Tools then appear as `x_<name>_<tool>`.

labels.description: Extra labels on the MCPServer CR.

name.description: MCPServer CR name (drives the tool prefix).

targetUrl.description: The muster MCP URL composed into an agent placed on a workload cluster (create_agent with organization and cluster): one those clusters reach, the installation's public muster endpoint. Empty refuses target clusters.

url.description: The platform's muster MCP URL, composed into every agent as the chart value `muster.url` (the URL of the agent's own RemoteMCPServer). Empty composes nothing and the Generic chart's default applies (`http://muster.agent-platform.svc.cluster.local:8090/mcp`). The `agent-platform` meta chart forwards it from its connectivity helper.

allowInternet.description: Allow egress on 443 to every destination: the chart registry (schema and version), GitHub (skill discovery and commit resolution) and the registries of OCI skills (digest resolution). Vanilla NetworkPolicy cannot select by name; narrow with egressCIDRs instead when the addresses are known.

allowKubeAPI.description: Allow egress to the Kubernetes API server.

enabled.description: Create a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for the pod (off when an umbrella chart renders the policies).

ingressNamespaces.description: Namespaces allowed to reach the API (label kubernetes.io/metadata.name). Empty allows ingress from the release namespace only.

metricsNamespaces.description: Namespaces allowed to scrape the metrics port (label kubernetes.io/metadata.name), when `observability.metrics.enabled`.

allowPublicClientRegistration.description: Accept unauthenticated dynamic client registration (labs only).

baseURL.description: Public base URL of this server: the issuer of its own OAuth metadata (https, or http on loopback). Empty derives `https://<fullname>.<global.domain>` when `global.domain` is set.

allowPrivateURLs.description: Let the issuer resolve to a private or loopback address (an in-cluster Dex).

caSecret.description: Secret with the CA of a Dex that serves a private certificate; `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `global.identity.ca.key`.

clientID.description: Dex OAuth client ID. Empty falls back to `global.identity.clientId`.

issuerURL.description: Dex issuer URL. Empty falls back to `global.identity.issuerUrl`.

enabled.description: Call the Kubernetes API as the caller: everything a request does (HelmReleases and OCIRepositories, the Agents, RemoteMCPServers, Harnesses, ModelConfigs and events it reads) presents the caller's IdP token, so the caller's RBAC governs — the apiserver must trust the IdP and the token's audience (a Dex install lists that audience in `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences`; a Google install's client id permissions: the chart renders none of its Roles (`rbac.create` is moot) and the token stays mounted only for the in-cluster API address and CA plus API discovery at startup, which every authenticated principal may read. agent-manager has no background work, so nothing is lost: a request without a token is refused with 401 instead of running as the ServiceAccount.

Make agent-manager an OAuth 2.1 resource server (mcp-oauth): the MCP endpoint and the REST API require a bearer token the platform identity provider issued, and every call carries the caller's identity (logged on every write, returned as `requestedBy`). On the Agent Platform muster forwards the session's IdP id_token to this server (MCPServer `auth.forwardToken`, rendered below) and the portal sends the signed-in user's id_token through the gateway; both are validated against the IdP's JWKS when their audience is in `trustedAudiences`. Off: anonymous, acting as the ServiceAccount — only for a server nothing but a trusted proxy can reach.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the provider credentials: `dex-client-secret` (dex) or `google-client-secret` (+ optional `google-client-id`) (google). Empty falls back to `global.identity.existingSecret`, whose `dex-client-secret` is the platform client's; without that, the chart renders a Secret from the values above.

clientID.description: Google OAuth client ID (not secret; may also come from the Secret key `google-client-id` when empty).

allowPrivateIPs.description: Let the IdP's JWKS endpoint resolve to a private address when validating forwarded tokens (an in-cluster Dex).

trustedAudiences.description: OAuth client IDs whose IdP id_tokens are accepted as bearer tokens (SSO token forwarding). Empty falls back to `[global.identity.clientId]`, the platform client MCP clients and the muster CLI log in with. The server trusts the union of this list and `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences` (in that order, without duplicates): every token muster forwards carries the required audiences by construction and they are what the kube-apiserver trusts, so a portal session — whose id_token carries them but not the platform client — is accepted without listing its client here.

enabled.description: Serve Prometheus metrics on `GET /metrics` of the `metrics` port: `mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds` per tool, and `http_server_request_duration_seconds` for the REST API and the MCP endpoint. Off, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none`: nothing is served, and nothing is pushed to `observability.otel.endpoint` either.

port.description: Port of the metrics listener, apart from the API port so an HTTPRoute or the OAuth guard never covers it.

endpoint.description: OTLP collector URL for traces, e.g. `http://otlp-gateway.kube-system.svc:4317` (gRPC) or `https://tempo.example.com:4318` (with protocol `http/protobuf`). Empty exports nothing; inbound `traceparent` headers still propagate. With `networkPolicy.enabled` the policy opens egress to it: the Service's namespace for an in-cluster host, every address otherwise.

headers.description: OTLP headers (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`), e.g. `X-Scope-OrgID=giantswarm` for a multi-tenant collector.

resourceAttributes.description: Resource attributes appended to the downward-API `k8s.pod.name`, `k8s.namespace.name` and `k8s.node.name`, e.g. `deployment.environment=glean`.

sampler.description: `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`. The parent-based default follows the caller's sampling decision and samples `samplerArg` of the traces that start here.

create.description: Create the Role/RoleBinding in `kagent.namespace` (and every `kagent.additionalNamespaces` entry): HelmReleases and OCIRepositories read/write; Agents, RemoteMCPServers, Harnesses, ModelConfigs and events read (Agents and RemoteMCPServers also delete, for the forced removal of what a suspended or bare release leaves behind) — the ServiceAccount's own permissions. Ignored with `oauth.downstream.enabled`: the ServiceAccount then gets no RBAC at all, the caller's RBAC governs.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas. The service is stateless (every read goes to the API server); more than one is fine.

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Number of old ReplicaSets retained for rollback. Keep tight so frequent rollouts don't leak zero-replica ReplicaSets across the cluster (each one still carries the pod template of an older chart version, and a Kyverno background scan reports every stale ReplicaSet that fails a newer policy).

enabled.description: Render a ServiceMonitor for the `metrics` port. Also needs `observability.metrics.enabled`; the meta chart turns this on with the tenant label.

interval.description: Scrape interval; empty uses the Prometheus Operator default.

labels.description: Labels on the ServiceMonitor, beside the chart's own. The Giant Swarm observability platform routes a scrape to a Mimir tenant by `observability.giantswarm.io/tenant`; a monitor without it writes to no tenant.

cacheTTL.description: How long a repository's discovered skills are reused.

gitAuthSecretName.description: Secret (key `token`) in the agents' namespace every agent with a git skill fetches its skills with at boot, unless the agent names its own `gitAuthSecretName`: composed as the agent chart's `skillsGitAuthSecretRef.name`. Empty: such agents fetch anonymously.

secretName.description: Existing Secret in the release namespace of the read-only skills GitHub App, with the keys `app-id`, `installation-id` and `private-key` (PEM): skills are discovered and pinned with the App's short-lived installation tokens, at the App's rate limit, and a private repository is offered to and usable by only the people who can read it themselves (their GitHub login, verified through the `github` pin below; without the pin private repositories are refused). Mutually exclusive with `tokenSecret`.

key.description: Key of the token in that Secret.

name.description: Existing Secret in the release namespace with a static GitHub token for skill discovery and pinning. Prefer `app`. Empty (and no `app`): anonymous, public repositories only.

mintGitAuthSecret.description: Boot private git skills with the skills GitHub App instead of a provisioned token (needs `github.app.secretName`; replaces `gitAuthSecretName`): the chart renders the Secret `<fullname>-skills-token` without data in `kagent.namespace` and every `kagent.additionalNamespaces` entry, plus a Role that may only get and update that Secret, and composes it as every git-skill agent's `skillsGitAuthSecretRef.name`. agent-manager writes an installation token into it (key `token`, the Basic form of `x-access-token:<token>`) and replaces it well before its one-hour expiry; `get_info` reports the last refresh and a failed one as `skillsGitAuthMint`.

repositories.description: GitHub repositories whose SKILL.md files list_skills offers (the same list the portal's create flow reads), each with the head commit an agent pins. Empty turns the skills capability off; skills given by URL are still resolved through the GitHub API.
